items.text: IRGC CLAIMS CAPTURE OF U.S. UNMANNED SUBMARINE Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy claims it captured a U.S. unmanned submarine near the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC said the operation relied on intelligence and operational planning, describing the vessel as an advanced autonomous submarine that entered U.S. service in 2025. Iran said the submarine remains in its possession and that images will be released later. The claim has not been independently verified.

KREMLIN HOPES US-BROKERED UKRAINE TALKS RESUME SOON The Kremlin says it hopes US-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine will restart soon, after negotiations stalled in February. Spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined to discuss possible terms of a settlement. His comments came after Presidents Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump spoke by phone Tuesday about prospects for ending the war in Ukraine.

KREMLIN: EUROPE FEELING PAIN OF HIGHER GAS PRICES The Kremlin says Europe is suffering from soaring natural gas prices amid the Iran war and could cut costs by buying Russian gas. European gas prices recently reached their highest level since late 2022. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Europe was hurting itself by relying on expensive spot-market gas instead of cheaper Russian supplies.

PIMCO: HIGH BOND YIELDS CHALLENGE STOCKS PIMCO says bonds are becoming more attractive after global yields climbed to their highest levels in more than a decade. US aggregate bond yields are now around 5%, roughly matching equity earnings yields. PIMCO argues bonds can once again provide meaningful income and protection if growth weakens, making a more balanced mix of stocks and fixed income increasingly attractive.

IRAN EXPANDS MARITIME RESTRICTED ZONE Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said a new maritime restricted zone will extend from Chabahar into parts of the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea, with exact coordinates to be announced. The move follows Tehran’s earlier plans to establish restrictions beyond the Strait of Hormuz, potentially widening disruption to shipping across a critical global energy route.

US MORTGAGE DEMAND FALLS AS RATES HIT 6.85% US mortgage applications fell 2.7% last week, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association. Refinancing applications dropped 6.2%, while home-purchase applications slipped 0.2%. The average 30-year mortgage rate rose six basis points to 6.85%, adding further pressure on borrowers and the housing market.

IRGC: WE WILL HIT 20 TARGETS FOR EVERY 2 OR 3 STRUCK Iran’s Revolutionary Guards warned they would respond forcefully to further attacks, saying every two or three Iranian targets hit could trigger strikes on 20 enemy targets. The IRGC also demanded an end to hostilities, an Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon, an end to Yemen’s blockade and the release of $24 billion in frozen Iranian assets.

U.S. BANK LAUNCHES ITS OWN STABLECOIN U.S. Bank has successfully tested USBDC, its proprietary dollar-backed stablecoin, in a live cross-border payment between its North American and European operations. The transaction ran on the Stellar blockchain while remaining integrated with the bank’s compliance and risk systems. U.S. Bank is exploring stablecoin applications including 24/7 payments, liquidity management, cross-border treasury operations and faster settlement.

CENTRAL BANKS FOCUS ON FUEL PRICES AS INFLATION RISK Central banks are increasingly watching refining margins, or “crack spreads,” as fuel shortages push gasoline and diesel prices higher. Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said refined fuel prices may provide a better inflation signal than crude oil alone. Wars in Iran and Ukraine have disrupted refining and exports, widening diesel margins sharply. The BOE estimates higher energy costs could add 0.4 percentage points to inflation in the se

AI BOOM DRIVES S&P 500 EARNINGS HIGHER S&P 500 earnings estimates are rising sharply, fueled by AI investment and stronger-than-expected corporate results. About 86% of companies beat analyst expectations, the highest share since 2021. Wall Street now expects 32% earnings growth in 2026, up from 24% before second-quarter results. AI-linked companies including Alphabet and Amazon delivered major beats, while communication services, consumer stocks and energy also saw significant upgrades.

AAPL - APPLE SET TO UNVEIL $2,000+ FOLDABLE IPHONE Apple is expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone Wednesday, marking new CEO John Ternus’ first major product launch. The device could cost more than $2,000, making it Apple’s most expensive handset yet. IDC expects Apple to capture 40% of the foldable smartphone market by end-2027. Apple is also expected to delay cheaper iPhone updates until spring, focusing this launch on the foldable, Pro and Pro Max models.

NORTHWESTERN MUTUAL: HOT CPI COULD TRIGGER FED HIKE Northwestern Mutual’s Matt Stucky says hotter-than-expected inflation could increase the chances of a Fed rate hike this month. Markets currently see roughly a 50-50 chance of a hike. Friday’s core CPI is expected to rise 0.2% month-over-month. A stronger reading, combined with the resilient U.S. labor market, could push the Fed toward tightening as policymakers focus on persistent inflation.

KUWAIT OFFERS OIL TRANSFERS OUTSIDE HORMUZ Kuwait Petroleum Corp is offering ship-to-ship transfers of crude oil and refined fuels outside the Strait of Hormuz as buyers avoid ports inside the waterway due to U.S.-Iran war risks. KPC says vessels will continue passing through Hormuz when conditions are safe. Kuwait’s naphtha exports have been heavily disrupted, recently running at around half their pre-war levels. Qatar, the UAE and Iraq are also offering oil from ports outside Hormuz.

COPPER HITS RECORD AS GLOBAL SUPPLIES TIGHTEN Copper hit a fresh record of $14,802.50 a ton, as tight supplies outside the U.S. outweighed concerns over Middle East tensions and slowing growth. LME copper has surged about 25% since March, driven partly by large metal flows into the U.S. ahead of potential tariffs. Some analysts see copper reaching $15,000 soon. Oil above $100 remains a key risk to global demand.

TRUMP PROMISES $5,000 DIVIDEND IF GOP WINS MIDTERMS President Donald Trump pledged a $5,000 payment to every adult U.S. citizen if Republicans retain control of Congress in November. Trump credited U.S. economic performance for the proposal, which would cost more than $1 trillion. He also urged supporters to “pretend that I’m on the ballot,” effectively framing the midterms as a referendum on his presidency. Trump said oil prices would fall once the war with Iran ends.

HOUTHIS SEIZE STRATEGIC RED SEA CITY Iran-backed Houthis have seized Yemen’s Mocha, according to Reuters sources. The advance brings the group closer to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, raising risks for Red Sea shipping and global trade.

HUAWEI HIKES AI CHIP PRICES 60% Huawei has reportedly raised the price of its Ascend 950DT AI accelerator by about 60% to $37,300, as booming demand outstrips supply. HBM shortages are adding to costs, while demand for Chinese alternatives to Nvidia continues to surge.

PUTIN AIDE: EUROPE DOES NOT WANT UKRAINE PEACE Putin aide Nikolay Patrushev claimed Western Europe is not interested in peace in Ukraine or encouraging Kyiv to negotiate. He said the U.S. appears more interested in negotiations, expressing hope Washington could push Kyiv toward talks.

META - JPMORGAN TURNS BULLISH ON META’S AI POTENTIAL JPMorgan upgraded Meta to Overweight and raised its price target to $820 from $640, implying roughly 24% upside. The bank sees significant new revenue opportunities from AI agents, subscriptions and enterprise AI services beyond advertising.

Bloomberg reports Tehran remains committed to fighting and has rebuilt missile capabilities, while the WSJ says top White House advisers have warned Trump the war could potentially last through 2029. HOUTHIS CLOSE IN ON KEY RED SEA CHOKEPOINT Iran-aligned Houthis have seized Yemen’s port city of Mocha and are pushing toward Dhubab and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, according to Reuters sources. Control of the strategic waterway could allow the group to further disrupt global shipping and Saudi oil exports, particularly as Hormuz remains constrained. Brent crude remained above $100 as risks to both major Middle East energy routes intensify.

TRUMP TOUTS “SOLD OUT” GOP MIDTERM CONVENTION President Donald Trump claimed the Republican Midterm Convention in Dallas drew record attendance and stronger overall viewership than the NFL. Trump said thousands were unable to enter the packed arena and announced he will return tonight to deliver the convention’s closing remarks.

ECB HIKES RATES 25 BPS AS INFLATION RISKS RISE The ECB raised rates by 25 basis points, taking the deposit rate to 2.50%, as the Middle East conflict keeps inflation pressures elevated. The ECB now sees inflation averaging 3.0% in 2026, 2.5% in 2027 and 2.1% in 2028, with the latter two forecasts revised higher. Growth forecasts were also upgraded, while the ECB stressed that future rate decisions remain data-dependent with no pre-set path.

WALL STREET SEES 5% TREASURY YIELD RISK A Reuters poll found 17 of 31 bond strategists see the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield potentially hitting 5% within three months. The 10-year recently reached 4.86%, pressured by $100+ oil, inflation concerns and heavy government borrowing. Strategists still forecast yields eventually falling, but conviction is weakening as Fed hike expectations and fiscal concerns rise.
